## Problem

## Requirements

- Input: a list of integers, with repeated entries allowed.
- Output: return the second-lowest number among values whose frequency in the list is exactly one.
- When fewer than two values occur only once, the expected result is unspecified and should be discussed with the interviewer (common choices include throwing an error, returning `null`, or returning `-1`).

## Notes

- Watch for short inputs with fewer than two elements, arrays made entirely of duplicates, and negative integers; do not presume every value is positive.

## Preparation

- For additional practice, review LC 215, "Kth Largest Element," to refresh quickselect; interviewers may sometimes present it as a broader variant.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Think of the problem as a two-pass filtering: first find all elements that appear exactly once, then find the second smallest among them.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Use a hash map to count frequencies in one pass, then iterate through the original list (or a sorted set of unique values) to find the two smallest with count 1.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

Complexity target: O(N) time and O(N) space, the edge case is when fewer than two unique elements exist—decide on a sentinel value or error handling upfront.

</details>
